# The Proposal

## Overview

I will improve Arity's analysis of package code, extend its metadata for
dependencies, and test these changes together in complete editing workflows.

## Detail

### Minimum Viable Product

1. **Language-server reliability.** I will improve Arity's handling of shared
   and inherited roxygen documentation. References, renaming, and call hierarchy
   will handle quoted function names consistently. Renaming will produce valid R
   syntax, including in infix calls, or Arity will refuse the operation.

2. **Package knowledge for editor assistance.** I will publish versioned indexes
   for at least 100 CRAN packages meeting the quality criteria below. These will
   include packages outside the existing bundle and dependencies used in the
   evaluation workflows. The indexes will contain exported names, symbol kinds,
   recoverable function arguments and defaults, and help. Arity will use these
   indexes to provide completion, hover information, and signature help without
   requiring local package installation.

   I will document the schema, automate weekly updates, and add a prefetch
   command for downloading indexes in bulk. The editor and CLI will use the same
   cached metadata and work with downloads disabled. Network access will remain
   an explicit user choice. Each index will record the package version and how
   the metadata was extracted.

3. **Validation and adoption.** I will test complete editing workflows on ten
   packages with cross-file references, imports, shared documentation, and
   nonstandard evaluation. These tests will also compare diagnostics from the
   editor and CLI. I will update the guides for VS Code, Positron, Neovim, and
   continuous integration (CI), explaining how to use Arity alongside other R
   tools and how to work offline.

Each behavior change will have regression tests and tests for cases that should
remain unchanged. I will build on Arity's existing corpus checks, protocol
tests, and benchmarks.

### Architecture

Arity analyzes code across a project and updates its analysis as files change.
Its architecture for parsing, formatting, and language intelligence is inspired
by [rust-analyzer](https://rust-analyzer.github.io/). The separately published
[`arity-parser`](https://crates.io/crates/arity-parser) and
[`arity-formatter`](https://crates.io/crates/arity-formatter) libraries are
already used by [`mini-roxygen-core`](https://github.com/eitsupi/mini-roxygen),
which generates R documentation and NAMESPACE files from roxygen comments.

Arity's metadata harvester already reads serialized R objects and
installed-package help without running R. Its binary parsing and Rd decoding
overlap with
[r-documentation-rs](https://github.com/eitsupi/r-documentation-rs). I will
coordinate with its maintainer to consolidate these readers in
r-documentation-rs, reducing duplication and making improvements available to
other R tools. Arity will continue to handle package discovery, export
resolution, metadata indexing, caching, and editor integration.

As of September 2026, Arity bundles export names for over 500 packages and has a
workflow to refresh them weekly. The remote client already supports downloads,
disk caching, and versioned indexes, but accepts only exported names. I will add
a pipeline to publish richer indexes, extend the client to supply signatures and
help, and make cached exports available to the CLI. Local indexes will take
precedence, and Arity will show the package version when it uses a remote index.

### Assumptions

Static analysis cannot determine what every name refers to at runtime. Arity
will refuse uncertain rewrites, and I will document unsupported cases. Remote
indexes describe current releases, which may differ from the versions a project
uses.

The main risks are incorrect or incomplete metadata, confusion between package
versions, and errors when renaming quoted function names. I will record missing
fields and failed extractions, and older metadata will retain the version of the
package it describes. I will keep the work within budget by selecting packages
and using existing infrastructure. Historical package versions and signatures
that require running R are outside the scope of this project.

### External Dependencies

For the pilot, I will extract metadata from unpacked [R-universe binary
packages](https://docs.r-universe.dev/install/binaries.html), falling back on
packages installed in CI when needed. I will check the complete export lists and
samples of signatures and help against the same package versions in R, and use
roxygen2 to check documentation behavior. These checks will use R, but users
will not need a running R session or installed dependencies to use the resulting
metadata. The source packages and extracted data will retain their version and
license information.

I am responsible for delivering the project, and the budget does not assume
development time from other maintainers. The work does not require changes to R.
